x: Pride of place, however, must go to Wil Wesch who joined us six months ago and has become the club's fastest 10 miler and our first winner of the Garnet since Ray Middleton in 1959.
Once again our boys managed to get among the handicap prizes Wil Wesch taking third individual and helping the A team into second handicap position behind Brighton.

First Chamionship win for Wil Wesch, Bob Coates and Paul Duckett filling the minor placings. Wil's time was not as fast as usual "taking it easy" but Paul walked a stormer to come through strongly over the later stages.
Wil Wesch shot into an early lead but after 1 mile he was joined by John and Ray and this group stayed together until the closing stages when John moved away strongly for a convincing win.

The spotlight however was on the superlative display of Wil Wesch who thrashed a much fancied Dave Watson to take the individual honours. As usual Wil started fast and moved easily until the last lap when he took the rest of the field to the cleaners with a sustained burst of high speed walking.
LEFT: Wil Wesch wins the Surrey 10 miles Championship. RIGHT: Lionel Mann finishes 168th in the National Championships
On the Belgrave course for the Surrey '10' our boys were edged out over the second half of the race although we provided the individual winner Wil Wesch.

On a not very good day W.Wesch took his first club championship. Tucking in behind early leaders Len Duquemin and Ray Middleton,Wil was content to let it go for the first 15 miles but when he made his move there was no response and he finished very strongly well clear of a struggling Middleton.
So worried were we by reports of the severity of the course and wild rumours of ropes and ice-axes that we sent out our scout Wil Wesch who travelled up a week early in order to be fully prepared.

Using this race as a warm up for the National Championships in June Belgrave placed four in the first sixteen to win comfortably from Bristol. In pouring rain only Wil Wesch went well to head the team in fourth individual position.
Nearly a clean sweep for Belgrave in the Surrey County Track Walks. The senior was won by Paul Nihill from Wil Wesch, Paul Duckett took the junior and Andy Hinchcliff walked off with the youth title.

Colin Gillett and Chris Martin took silver and bronze in the 200 metres, both in 22.9, and Chris also finished third in the 100 metres (11.5). Our only other senior medal winner was Wil Wesch who took second place behind a National record-breaking Nihill in the 3,000 metres walk.

Harry turned out to put a critical eye over the last 3,000 metres of the season (won by Wil Wesch in the fastest time by a Belgravian this year - 12.50.6) and then pushed the boys along the Hastings-Brighton road.

Carl Lawton has really shaken off his recent lack of form and he finished fifth close on Wil Wesch's heels. Scoring five a side Belgrave had little trouble in defeating Surrey with evergreen Percy Wilson making a rare first team appearance.

Stage 2 saw Wil Wesch put Leicester back behind Belgrave A with a determined display of fast walking. Dave Dorey of Sarnia made a guest appearance for the B team bringing them in third 1½ minutes up on Southend.

Bert East (centre) had difficulty in even making the start of the London Transport '2' on July 6th at Acton, but mention the word "handicap" and he's off like a shot! Ray Middleton thinks it's a laugh beating the 2 miles record of a No.11 bus, while Wil Wesch gets on with winning at well over speed-limit

Fast walking by Wil Wesch and Len Duquemin put Ray Middleton back in third place although he did take the Civil Service 7 Mile title. Bob Coates was another to excel on this fast course putting Carl Lawton back to fifth man for Belgrave.
In a 3,000 metres walk at Crystal Palace on October 25th WIL WESCH led American Olympian Ron Laird to the half distance before conceding victory 13:01.0 to 13:14.2.
By the end of the first lap the field had stretched right out with Colin and Lightman locked together closely followed by Oliveros, Ramirez Wil Wesch and Bob Coates who were both walking superbly.
Wil Wesch (31) in action during the 'Open' 7.
It was a great wedding party at John's local H.Q. - South London Harriers, Coulsdon - and things can expect to be livened up in the Chipstead Valley area pretty soon. To WIL WESCH on his marriage.
Wil Wesch looks a proud man as he gazes at the Tommy Green Cup, which he received at the Club Dinner and Dance at the Wimbledon Hill Hotel on November 21.

Our lads dominate the walks, with Wil Wesch top of the 20,000m. and Ray Middleton top of the 50,000m. Wil also has second in the 10,000m. and third in the 3,000m., while Ray has 25th in the 3,000m., 14th in the 10,000m., and 27th in the 20,000m.

Wil Wesch surrandered his 3,000m. walk title to in-form Paul Nihill, but in doing so helped his rival to a new world best performance. Bob Coates showed good form after a spell away from competition to take third place, and with Carl Lawton fourth and Dave DeBondi sixth, it was a pity there was no team race.
Contributing to Surrey's victory was Wil Wesch, who took fourth place in the 10,000m. walk on the Saturday in 45m. 02.2s., and third in the 3,000m. walk on the Monday in 12m. 33.4s.
Last year's winner, our very own Wil Wesch, was sixth. This may seem pretty small beer for Wil, but it represents a good performance.
With Wil Wesch back in the side, and Ray Middleton back with the leaders, we scored a clear win. And contributing to our victory was a particularly bright performance by young Alan Callow.
WIL WESCH, who was the life and soul of Belgrave walking teams last year, is now back in Germany. His efforts during the year earned him a place in West Germany's 20 kilometres walk team.
WIL WESCH (1), selected for West Germany in the 20 Kilos walk at the Olympic Games, Munich 1972, leads British international Paul Nihill in the Surrey County 3,000m track championship of 1971.
